## Findings
- claim-1: The original conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 families \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), are minimal. [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The 2024 paper defines \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), works integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and proves minimality of the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- claim-3: The same paper proves no homogeneous syzygy of the required form and concludes that the lower-adjoined family is minimal. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
- claim-4: For the other, right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), the paper states only that its elements are conjugates of the proved family and says one “could” transpose the arguments; this passage is not itself a proof of that family’s minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]
- claim-5: Assuming accepted tasks `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1` and `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1`, partition conjugation gives an integral graded isomorphism from the quotient for \((r,q,i,j)\) to that for \((q,r,j,i)\), sends the right-adjoined family to the lower-adjoined family, and therefore proves right-family minimality from the certified lower-family result.
- claim-6: A fresh independent adversarial review certifying that the accepted conjugation/descent proof has no missing parameter, ideal-descent, or minimality-transfer hypothesis is not present in the supplied immutable record.
## Strategy
Audit outcome: the original conjecture requires minimality of **both** families [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]. The 2024 source proves the lower-adjoined family integrally, with exact parameters and quotient [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235], and proves its minimality by no-syzygies [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]. It does not prove the right-adjoined family: it says its arguments “could” be transposed [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840].

The strongest possible completion is conjugation. Put \(q=n-r\) and
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee,n)=(q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n).
\]
The required certificate must prove admissibility, derive
\[
(i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b),
\]
and show integrally that \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), and
\[
\omega(G_R(v))=G_L(v^\vee).
\]
Then lower-family minimality transfers to \(G_R\), and the Grassmannian result transfers to the original flag-variety basic ideal using [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 207-211]. No transition identity is needed.

## Gaps
The requested target is **not established in the current immutable record**. Ledger claim-5, the decisive conjugation/descent implication, remains unsupported; claim-6 records that no fresh independent adversarial review exists.

In particular, accepted internal task references do not replace a dependency-closed certificate proving:
\[
1\le t^\vee\le r^\vee,s^\vee\le n,\qquad
t^\vee>r^\vee+s^\vee-n,
\]
the Schur-basis ideal descent, the exact right-to-lower family bijection, the \(a=0\) case, and irredundancy transfer.

## Next
Proposed narrow certificate task:

> Prove and independently adversarially review the standalone conjugation transfer for \(G_R\): from \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), verify admissibility of \((q,q-i+j,q-i+1,n)\); derive \((j,i,a,b)\); prove basiswise \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\), \(\omega(J_v)=J_{v^\vee}\), and \(\omega(G_R(v))=G_L(v^\vee)\), including \(a=0\); transfer lower-family minimality and then invoke [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 207-211].

Only a successful independent review of that certificate could close the original two-family minimality conjecture.
